assessments.reasoning: The original title leaf shows May 1964 First Draft. The original preface identifies BASIC as the response to Dartmouth's time-sharing needs, including ease of learning and general-purpose use. The facing facsimile note is signed August 2000.

challenge.method: Read both leaves in the same spread and the original preface visually. Compare Dartmouth's later institutional history and the two ECMA Brief History pages. Check whether the frozen statement requires an actual first release date.
challenge.results: The manual's date and the modern reprint note have different roles. ECMA-55 gives 1964 as the first-version year while ECMA-116 literally gives June 1965. The witnesses do not resolve that origin-date conflict, and the proposal states the purpose of the named manual rather than a launch chronology.

limitations: The original title and preface support this manual-specific identity. The exact date of first operational release and later interpretations are separate questions.
